high.title: Apple to Launch Two Foldable Phones, Major Suppliers Including TSMC, Hon Hai Set to Accelerate Q2 Inventory Build-Up
high.summary: Foreign media reports suggest Apple's first foldable iPhone may launch with two models this year - a "large and small foldable" strategy to capture market share. Apple appears confident about iPhone Fold sales, with supply chain expected to accelerate inventory build-up in late Q2/early Q3. Key beneficiaries include Hon Hai (2317), TSMC (2330), Largan Precision (3008), and Sintai Optical (3376). Industry sources indicate Apple may adopt Samsung's successful dual-model approach, directly competing across same price segments. The larger model features an approximately 7.5-8 inch internal screen with book-style inward folding design, while the smaller model resembles a compact mirror flip design. This represents a significant product expansion for Apple and could drive substantial revenue growth for Taiwan's supply chain partners, particularly given Apple's focus on reducing screen crease depth to below 0.15mm, requiring advanced manufacturing capabilities.

high.title: Oil Price Surge Creates Four Categories of War-Beneficiary Stocks with Taiwan Polymer, Swancor Holdings Attracting Buying Interest
high.summary: Middle East warfare has driven international oil prices near $120/barrel, spurring buying interest in four major sectors: petrochemicals and derivatives, paper manufacturing, oil/gas/electricity, and shipping. Sixteen "war-beneficiary stocks" including Taiwan Polymer (1304) and Taiwan SynCorr (1309) have shown strong performance as market focuses on defensive plays. PE prices have surged 37% since the US-Iran conflict began, rising from RMB 6,597/ton to RMB 8,990/ton by March 27th. Cultural and industrial paper prices are also trending upward with 10% increases announced by major paper manufacturers. The oil price rally directly impacts upstream petrochemical feedstock costs, benefiting companies with low-cost inventory holdings who can capture significant inventory gains. This trend supports Taiwan Polymer, Acelon Chemical & Fiber, and other PE manufacturers who can benefit from the price-cost spread dynamics.
